reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more targeted approach to developing key physiological adaptations. While Plan B includes longer runs, it focuses heavily on endurance and doesn't dedicate sufficient time to high-intensity interval training, which is crucial for improving speed. Plan A’s inclusion of dedicated threshold intervals and a balanced mix of aerobic work and recovery allows for a more effective build-up of both aerobic capacity and the ability to sustain faster paces. Furthermore, the shorter, more frequent hard sessions in Plan A are likely to be more manageable and less taxing on the body than the longer, more demanding sessions in Plan B.
